text.p: The sorghum market remains subdued with limited trade being reported from either growers or consumers, Queensland co-operative Grainco Ltd said in its weekly market report.

Both appear comfortable to stand aside from the market, watching the progress of the winter plant in Queensland and New South Wales (NSW) for longer-term price direction of sorghum compared with wheat and barley.
South Queensland bids finished the week around A$143.00 per tonne delivered Brisbane, with the southern markets in NSW and Victoria offering no opportunities in the short-term.
In central Queensland, prices finished the week unchanged at A$121.00 a tonne delivered port, with little fresh news other than continuing good progress of the U.S. corn crop.
Recent good weather in Europe and Canada has given the new crop barley values a bearish tone, with the harvest in Europe beginning in two weeks.

In Australia, forecast El Nino dry weather has produced mixed planting prospects in southern regions. Significant rainfall is still needed in eastern and southern Australia to complete barley planting.
Domestic feed barley values finished the week unchanged at A$175.00 a tonne delivered Brisbane for June/July, reflecting a premium over export values which are softer at around US$140.00 a tonne fob.
New crop values finished the week at A$153.00 a tonne Brisbane for November-December delivery.
Domestic new crop malting barley prices finished the week at around A$183.00 a tonne delivered port.
On a more active cottonseed export front, firm enquiries were received from Korea and Japan for cottonseed for prompt shipment through to the 1998 new crop.
Prices for containerised product are still well below six weeks ago.
Despite two cargoes of seed committed for bulk export, traditional container consumers believe prices should weaken as the supply of Australian seed remains plentiful.
Mediocre domestic feed offtake, softer crushing margins and a delay in the crush uptake all support this view.
However, export consumers are failing to see that available seed is being aggregated in strong hands.
The power of export consumers are not to be understimated.
They are very good at manipulating the market to suit their requirements and Australian marketers will need to maintain a strong price stance across the board in order to work prices higher.
Cash prices continued around A$145.00 to A$150.00 Downs gin to the grower.
In central Queensland prices have firmed to A$150.00 ex gin for ginning period delivery to domestic consumers.
It was another quiet week in the pulse market.
Planting continues across much of northern NSW for late June and if rain is received in time is likely to see those acres originally intended for pulses go into the ground.
Many forecasts are predicting late frosts which may favour later plantings in many areas.
Price indications for the new crop continue at around the A$310.00 to A$315.00 a tonne delivered port for Queensland chickpeas and faba beans at around A$250.00 port for the new crop.
Domestic oilseed values were slightly higher with sunflowers finishing the week at A$317.00 a tonne Brisbane crushed for June/July and A$327.00 a tonne Newcastle for June/July.
Central Queensland sunflower prices finished steady at A$272.00-A$277.00 a tonne central Queensland depot for June/July.
New crop soybean prices moved lower to A$420.00 a tonne Brisbane.
